question_text: What is the output? String a="Java"; String b="Java"; System.out.println(a==b);
explanation: Identical string literals are reused from the String pool.

question_text: Which statement about StringBuffer is correct?
explanation: StringBuffer is mutable, so its contents can be changed.

question_text: Which method adds text at the end of a StringBuffer?
explanation: append() adds the supplied value at the end of a StringBuffer.

question_text: What is the output? StringBuffer sb=new StringBuffer("Java"); sb.append(" SE"); System.out.println(sb);
explanation: append() modifies the existing StringBuffer by adding SE.

question_text: Which method inserts text at a specified position in a StringBuffer?
explanation: insert(index, value) inserts text at the specified position.

question_text: What is the output? StringBuffer sb=new StringBuffer("Java"); sb.reverse(); System.out.println(sb);
explanation: reverse() reverses the character sequence to avaJ.

question_text: Which method removes characters from a StringBuffer between two indexes?
explanation: delete(start,end) removes characters from start up to but excluding end.

question_text: Which method returns the current capacity of a StringBuffer?
explanation: capacity() returns the current allocated character capacity.

question_text: What is the output? StringBuffer sb=new StringBuffer("Hello"); System.out.println(sb.length());
explanation: The buffer contains five characters.

question_text: What is the output? StringBuffer sb=new StringBuffer("Code"); sb.setCharAt(0,'N'); System.out.println(sb);
explanation: setCharAt() replaces the character at index 0, producing Node.

question_text: Which statement is true about StringBuffer and String?
option_b: StringBuffer is mutable and String is immutable
option_c: String is mutable and StringBuffer is immutable
explanation: StringBuffer can be modified, whereas String objects cannot be changed.

question_text: Which keyword is used to define a class in Java?
explanation: The class keyword defines a class.

question_text: Which keyword is commonly used to create an object?
explanation: The new operator creates an object and invokes its constructor.

question_text: What is the purpose of the dot operator in Java?
option_b: To access members of an object
explanation: The dot operator accesses fields and methods through an object reference.

question_text: Where are instance variables declared?
option_b: Inside a class but outside methods
explanation: Instance variables are declared in the class body and belong to objects.

question_text: Where is a local variable declared?
explanation: A local variable is declared within a method, constructor, or block.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { int x=10; } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){ Test t=new Test(); System.out.println(t.x); }}
explanation: The object t accesses the instance variable x, whose value is 10.

question_text: Which part of a method declaration specifies the value returned by the method?
explanation: The return type specifies the type of value a method returns.

question_text: What is the output? class A { int add(int a,int b){return a+b;} } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){ A obj=new A(); System.out.println(obj.add(3,4)); }}
explanation: The method returns 3 + 4, which is 7.

question_text: How is an instance method normally called from another class using an object?
explanation: An instance method is called using an object reference and the dot operator.

question_text: What is a constructor in Java?
option_a: A method with any return type
option_b: A special member used to initialize objects
explanation: A constructor initializes an object when it is created.

question_text: Which statement about a constructor is correct?
option_a: It must have the same name as its class
explanation: A constructor has the same name as its class and has no return type.

question_text: What happens if no constructor is declared in a class?
explanation: The compiler supplies a default no-argument constructor when no constructor is declared.

question_text: Which constructor accepts arguments?
explanation: A parameterized constructor accepts values to initialize an object.

question_text: What is the output? class A { A(){System.out.println("Created");} } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){ new A(); }}
explanation: Creating the object invokes its no-argument constructor.

question_text: What is constructor overloading?
option_a: Defining constructors with different parameter lists
explanation: Constructor overloading provides multiple constructors with different parameter lists.

question_text: Which feature allows a class to have both A() and A(int x)?
explanation: The constructors have different parameter lists, so they are overloaded.

question_text: What does this refer to in an instance method?
explanation: this refers to the current object.

question_text: What is the output? class A { int x; A(int x){this.x=x;} } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){ A a=new A(15); System.out.println(a.x); }}
explanation: this.x refers to the instance variable, while x refers to the constructor parameter.

question_text: Where must a call to this() appear inside a constructor?
explanation: A constructor call using this() must be the first statement.

question_text: What is method overloading?
option_a: Same method name with different parameter lists
option_b: Same method name only in subclasses
explanation: Overloaded methods share a name but differ in parameter lists.

question_text: Can two methods be overloaded by changing only their return types?
explanation: Return type alone cannot distinguish overloaded methods.

question_text: What is the output? class A { int add(int a,int b){return a+b;} double add(double a,double b){return a+b;} } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){ A a=new A(); System.out.println(a.add(2,3)); }}
explanation: The integer version is selected and returns 5.

question_text: Which is a valid overloaded method pair?
option_a: void show(int x) and void show(String x)
option_b: int add(int x) and double add(int x)
explanation: Different parameter types allow valid method overloading.

question_text: Can an object reference be passed as a method argument in Java?
explanation: Java methods can accept object references as parameters.

question_text: What is the output? class A { int x; } public class Main { static void change(A a){a.x=20;} public static void main(String[] args){A obj=new A(); obj.x=5; change(obj); System.out.println(obj.x);}}
explanation: The method receives a copy of the reference to the same object and modifies its field.

question_text: What is passed to a method when an object is supplied as an argument?
explanation: Java passes the reference value by value; the method can access the same object.

question_text: What is the default value of an instance variable of type int?
explanation: Instance variables of type int receive the default value zero.

question_text: What happens if a local variable is used before initialization?
explanation: Local variables must be initialized before they are used.

question_text: What is wrong with this code? class Student { void Student(){System.out.println("Hello");} }
option_b: It is a method and not a constructor
explanation: A constructor has no return type. void makes Student() an ordinary method.

question_text: What is the output? class A { void show(int x){System.out.print("I");} void show(double x){System.out.print("D");} } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){new A().show(5);}}
explanation: The integer argument selects show(int), so I is printed.

question_text: What is the output? class A { int x=5; } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){ A[] arr=new A[2]; System.out.println(arr[0]); }}
explanation: An array of object references initially contains null references.

question_text: Which keyword is used to refer to the current object's instance variable when a parameter has the same name?
explanation: this distinguishes the instance variable from a local parameter with the same name.

question_text: Can a constructor be overloaded with different parameter types?
explanation: Constructors can have different parameter lists, including different parameter types.

question_text: What is the output? String[] names={"Ram","Sam"}; System.out.println(names[1]);
explanation: Index 1 refers to the second element, Sam.

question_text: What is inheritance in Java?
option_b: Acquiring properties and methods of another class
explanation: Inheritance allows a class to acquire accessible members of another class.

question_text: Which keyword is used to inherit a class in Java?
explanation: The extends keyword is used for class inheritance.

question_text: Which class is known as the parent class?
explanation: The class whose members are inherited is called the superclass.

question_text: Which class inherits properties from another class?
explanation: A subclass inherits accessible members from its superclass.

question_text: Which type of inheritance is directly supported between Java classes?
explanation: Java supports multilevel inheritance through class extension.

question_text: Does Java support multiple inheritance through classes?
explanation: A Java class cannot extend more than one class.

question_text: Which feature allows a subclass to reuse superclass methods?
explanation: Inheritance promotes code reuse by allowing subclasses to use inherited methods.

question_text: What is the output? class A { void show(){System.out.print("A");} } class B extends A {} public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){new B().show();}}
explanation: B inherits the show method from A and executes it.

question_text: What is the output? class A { int x=10; } class B extends A {} public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){B obj=new B(); System.out.println(obj.x);}}
explanation: The subclass object can access the inherited public or package-accessible field.

question_text: Which members are not directly inherited by a subclass?
explanation: Constructors are not inherited by subclasses.

question_text: Which keyword refers to the immediate superclass object context?
explanation: super is used to access superclass members and constructors.

question_text: What is the output? class A { A(){System.out.print("A");} } class B extends A { B(){System.out.print("B");} } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){new B();}}
explanation: The superclass constructor executes before the subclass constructor.

question_text: What happens when a subclass constructor does not explicitly call super()?
option_b: Compiler inserts a super() call when applicable
explanation: The compiler inserts an implicit no-argument super() call when applicable.

question_text: Which statement about Java inheritance is correct?
option_a: A class can extend many classes
option_b: A class can extend one class
explanation: Java classes have only one direct superclass.

question_text: What is multilevel inheritance?
option_b: A class extends a class that already extends another class
explanation: Multilevel inheritance forms a chain of superclass and subclass relationships.

question_text: What is the output? class A { void show(){System.out.print("Hello");} } class B extends A {} class C extends B {} public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){new C().show();}}
explanation: C inherits show through B from A.

question_text: Which access modifier allows access from subclasses even when they are in different packages?
explanation: protected members are accessible in subclasses subject to Java access rules.

question_text: Can a private superclass field be directly accessed by its subclass?
explanation: Private members are not directly accessible in a subclass.

question_text: What is the purpose of the super keyword?
explanation: super provides access to superclass constructors and members.

question_text: Which statement about constructors in inheritance is correct?
option_b: Superclass constructor runs before subclass constructor
explanation: Superclass initialization occurs before subclass initialization.

question_text: What is the output? class A { int x=5; } class B extends A { int x=10; void show(){System.out.println(super.x);}} public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){new B().show();}}
explanation: super.x accesses the superclass field, whose value is 5.

question_text: What is method overriding?
option_a: Defining same method in unrelated classes
option_b: Redefining an inherited method in a subclass
explanation: Method overriding provides a subclass-specific implementation of an inherited method.

question_text: Which condition is required for method overriding?
option_a: Same method name and compatible parameters
explanation: An overriding method uses the same signature with a compatible return type.

question_text: What is the output? class A { void show(){System.out.print("A");} } class B extends A { void show(){System.out.print("B");} } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){new B().show();}}
explanation: The subclass version overrides the superclass method.

question_text: Can a static method be overridden in the same way as an instance method?
explanation: Static methods are hidden rather than overridden.

question_text: Which annotation is commonly used to indicate an overriding method?
explanation: The @Override annotation helps the compiler verify overriding.

question_text: Can an overriding method reduce the visibility of the inherited method?
explanation: An overriding method cannot have more restrictive access than the overridden method.

question_text: Can an overriding method use a covariant return type?
explanation: A covariant return type may be a subtype of the original method's return type.

question_text: What happens if a subclass method has the same name but different parameters?
explanation: Different parameter lists create an overloaded method rather than overriding.

question_text: What is dynamic method dispatch?
option_b: Runtime selection of an overridden method
explanation: The JVM selects the overridden instance method based on the actual object type at runtime.

question_text: What is the output? class A { void show(){System.out.print("A");} } class B extends A { void show(){System.out.print("B");} } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){A obj=new B(); obj.show();}}
explanation: The reference is A but the actual object is B, so B's overridden method executes.

question_text: In A obj = new B(), what determines the overridden instance method executed?
explanation: Dynamic dispatch uses the actual runtime object type.

question_text: Can dynamic method dispatch apply to overridden static methods?
explanation: Static methods are resolved using the reference or class type, not runtime dispatch.

question_text: What is the output? class A { void show(){System.out.print("A");} } class B extends A { void show(){System.out.print("B");} } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){A obj=new B(); ((A)obj).show();}}
explanation: Casting the reference to A does not change the actual object, which remains B.

question_text: What does super.show() call when show() is overridden in a subclass?
explanation: super.show() explicitly invokes the superclass implementation.

question_text: What is the output? class A { void show(){System.out.print("A");} } class B extends A { void show(){super.show(); System.out.print("B");} } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){new B().show();}}
explanation: The superclass method prints A first, followed by B.

question_text: What does final mean when applied to a class?
explanation: A final class cannot be subclassed.

question_text: What happens when a method is declared final?
explanation: A final method cannot be overridden by subclasses.

question_text: What is the output? final int x=10; x=20; System.out.println(x);
explanation: A final variable cannot be reassigned after initialization.

question_text: Can a final object reference point to a different object after initialization?
explanation: A final reference cannot be reassigned, although the referenced object's state may change.

question_text: Which keyword prevents a method from being overridden?
explanation: The final modifier prevents subclasses from overriding the method.

question_text: What is a static variable?
option_a: A variable created separately for every method
option_b: A class-level variable shared by instances
option_c: A variable that cannot be initialized
explanation: A static field belongs to the class and is shared by its instances.

question_text: How is a static variable commonly accessed?
explanation: A static variable can be accessed using the class name and dot operator.

question_text: What is the output? class A { static int count=0; A(){count++;} } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){new A(); new A(); System.out.println(A.count);}}
explanation: Both objects increment the same static variable, resulting in 2.

question_text: Which statement about a static method is correct?
option_a: It requires an object to be called
explanation: A static method belongs to the class rather than an individual object.

question_text: Can a static method directly access a non-static instance variable?
explanation: A static method has no current object reference and cannot directly access instance members.

question_text: What is the output? class A { static void show(){System.out.print("Java");} } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){A.show();}}
explanation: The static method is called directly using the class name.

question_text: When is a static initialization block generally executed?
option_a: Every time an object is created
explanation: A static block runs during class initialization.

question_text: What is the output? class A { static {System.out.print("Static ");} A(){System.out.print("Object");} } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){new A();}}
explanation: The static block runs during class initialization before the constructor.

question_text: Which keyword declares a nested class that does not require an enclosing object instance?
explanation: A static nested class does not need an instance of the outer class.

question_text: Can a static method be overloaded?
explanation: Static methods can have multiple versions with different parameter lists.

question_text: Which keyword is used to declare an abstract class?
explanation: The abstract keyword declares an abstract class.

question_text: Can an abstract class be instantiated directly?
explanation: An abstract class cannot be instantiated directly.

question_text: What is an abstract method?
option_b: A method with only local variables
explanation: An abstract method is declared without an implementation body.

question_text: Which class must implement inherited abstract methods unless it is also abstract?
explanation: A concrete subclass must provide implementations for inherited abstract methods.

question_text: Can an abstract class contain constructors and concrete methods?
explanation: Abstract classes can contain constructors, fields, and concrete methods.

question_text: What happens if a concrete subclass does not implement an inherited abstract method?
option_b: It must be declared abstract or compilation fails
explanation: A concrete class must implement all inherited abstract methods.

question_text: Can an abstract method be declared final?
explanation: An abstract method must be overridden, while final prevents overriding.

question_text: Can an abstract method be private?
explanation: A private method cannot be overridden by a subclass, so it cannot serve as an abstract method.

question_text: What is the output? abstract class A { abstract void show(); } class B extends A { void show(){System.out.print("Done");} } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){A obj=new B(); obj.show();}}
explanation: B implements show(), and dynamic dispatch executes that implementation.

question_text: Which statement best describes an abstract class?
option_a: It must contain only abstract methods
option_b: It can contain both abstract and concrete methods
explanation: An abstract class may provide partial implementation and shared state.

question_text: Which keyword is used to declare an interface?
explanation: The interface keyword declares an interface.

question_text: Which keyword is used by a class to implement an interface?
explanation: A class uses implements to provide an interface implementation.

question_text: Can a Java class implement multiple interfaces?
explanation: A class can implement multiple interfaces.

question_text: What is the default visibility of an interface field?
explanation: Interface fields are implicitly public, static, and final.

question_text: Which type of method is traditionally abstract by default in an interface?
explanation: An ordinary interface method without a body is implicitly public and abstract.

question_text: Can an interface extend another interface?
explanation: An interface can extend one or more interfaces.

question_text: Can an interface extend multiple interfaces?
explanation: An interface may extend multiple interfaces.

question_text: Can a class extend an interface directly?
explanation: A class implements an interface; it does not extend it.

question_text: What is the output? interface A { void show(); } class B implements A { public void show(){System.out.print("Hello");} } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){A obj=new B(); obj.show();}}
explanation: B implements the interface method, and the interface reference calls it.

question_text: Why must an implemented interface method generally be declared public?
explanation: The implementation cannot reduce the public visibility required by the interface.

question_text: Can an interface contain default methods with implementations?
explanation: Default methods allow interfaces to provide method implementations.

question_text: Which keyword identifies an interface default method?
explanation: The default keyword is used to declare a default interface method.

question_text: Can an interface contain static methods?
explanation: Interfaces can declare static methods with implementations.

question_text: How is a static interface method normally called?
explanation: Static interface methods are called using the interface name.

question_text: Can an interface have a constructor?
explanation: Interfaces cannot be instantiated and do not have constructors.

question_text: What happens if a class implements an interface but does not implement all its abstract methods?
option_b: It must be abstract or compilation fails
explanation: A non-abstract class must implement all inherited abstract methods.

question_text: What is the output? interface A { int X=10; } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){System.out.println(A.X);}}
explanation: Interface fields are public static final and can be accessed using the interface name.

question_text: Can an interface extend two interfaces named A and B?
explanation: An interface can extend multiple interfaces using a comma-separated list.

question_text: What is a nested interface?
option_a: An interface declared inside another type
explanation: A nested interface is declared within another class or interface.

question_text: Which relationship is represented when a class implements an interface?
explanation: Implementing an interface means the class agrees to provide the required behavior.

question_text: What does polymorphism mean in Java?
explanation: Polymorphism allows the same interface or method call to represent different behaviors.

question_text: Which feature is an example of compile-time polymorphism?
explanation: Method overloading is resolved at compile time.

question_text: Which feature is an example of runtime polymorphism?
explanation: Overridden instance methods are selected at runtime.

question_text: What is the output? class A { void show(){System.out.print("A");} } class B extends A { void show(){System.out.print("B");} } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){A x=new B(); x.show();}}
explanation: Runtime polymorphism selects the B implementation.

question_text: What is an upcasting operation?
option_a: Subclass reference assigned to superclass reference
option_b: Superclass reference assigned to unrelated class
explanation: Upcasting treats a subclass object through a superclass reference.

question_text: Is upcasting generally performed automatically in Java?
explanation: A subclass object can be assigned to a compatible superclass reference automatically.

question_text: What is downcasting?
option_a: Converting superclass reference to subclass reference
explanation: Downcasting explicitly converts a superclass reference to a subclass reference.

question_text: Which operator can check whether an object is an instance of a particular type?
explanation: instanceof checks whether an object is compatible with a specified type.

question_text: What happens when an invalid downcast is attempted at runtime?
explanation: An incompatible runtime cast can cause ClassCastException.

question_text: What is the output? class A {} class B extends A {} public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){A obj=new B(); System.out.println(obj instanceof B);}}
explanation: The actual object is an instance of B.

question_text: Can a superclass reference access a subclass-only method without casting?
explanation: The compiler checks accessible members using the reference's declared type.

question_text: What determines which overloaded method is selected?
option_b: Compile-time argument types and method signatures
explanation: Overload resolution is performed at compile time using argument types.

question_text: What is the output? class A { void show(int x){System.out.print("Int");} void show(double x){System.out.print("Double");} } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){new A().show(5);}}
explanation: The int argument selects show(int).

question_text: Can constructors be overridden?
explanation: Constructors are not inherited, so they cannot be overridden.

question_text: Can private methods be overridden by subclasses?
explanation: Private methods are not inherited as accessible methods and cannot be overridden.

question_text: What is the output? class A { int x=10; } class B extends A { int x=20; } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){A obj=new B(); System.out.println(obj.x);}}
explanation: Fields are hidden rather than dynamically dispatched; the reference type A determines the field accessed.

question_text: Can a final class implement an interface?
option_d: Only if it has no methods
explanation: final prevents subclassing but does not prevent interface implementation.

question_text: Can an abstract class implement an interface without implementing every method?
explanation: An abstract class may leave interface methods unimplemented for subclasses.

question_text: What happens if two implemented interfaces provide conflicting default methods with the same signature?
option_b: The class must resolve the conflict
option_d: The program always uses the first interface
explanation: The implementing class must override the conflicting default method.

question_text: How can a class explicitly call a particular interface's default method when resolving a conflict?
explanation: InterfaceName.super.method() invokes that interface's default implementation.

question_text: Which statement best describes the is-a relationship?
option_a: A subclass is a type of its superclass
explanation: Inheritance models an is-a relationship between a subclass and superclass.

question_text: What is a package in Java?
option_a: A collection of related classes and interfaces
explanation: A package groups related classes and interfaces.

question_text: Which keyword is used to declare a package?
explanation: The package keyword declares the package to which a class belongs.

question_text: Which keyword is used to import a class or package?
explanation: The import keyword allows access to types from other packages.

question_text: Which package is automatically imported into every Java source file?
explanation: java.lang is automatically imported by the Java compiler.

question_text: Which package contains the Scanner class?
explanation: Scanner belongs to the java.util package.

question_text: Where should a package declaration normally appear in a Java source file?
option_b: Before import statements and type declarations
explanation: The package declaration must be the first non-comment statement in a compilation unit.

question_text: What is the main advantage of using packages?
option_b: To organize related classes and avoid naming conflicts
explanation: Packages organize code and help prevent naming conflicts.

question_text: Which statement imports all accessible types from java.util?
explanation: The wildcard import makes accessible types in java.util available by simple name.

question_text: What is the output? import java.util.*; public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){ArrayList<Integer> a=new ArrayList<>(); a.add(10); System.out.println(a.get(0));}}
explanation: ArrayList stores the added integer, which is retrieved at index zero.

question_text: Can two classes have the same simple name if they belong to different packages?
explanation: Fully qualified names distinguish classes with the same simple name in different packages.

question_text: What is a fully qualified class name?
option_b: Package name followed by class name
explanation: A fully qualified name includes the package name and the class name.

question_text: Which command compiles a Java source file in a package directory structure?
explanation: javac is the Java compiler used to compile source files.

question_text: Which command runs a compiled Java class using its fully qualified name?
explanation: The java launcher runs a class using its fully qualified name.

question_text: What is the purpose of the CLASSPATH setting?
option_a: To specify where Java can find classes and packages
explanation: CLASSPATH helps Java locate user-defined classes and libraries.

question_text: Which access modifier allows access only within the same class?
explanation: private members are accessible only within their declaring class.

question_text: What is the default access level when no access modifier is specified?
explanation: Without an access modifier, members have package-private access.

question_text: Which access modifier provides the widest accessibility?
explanation: public members are accessible from any package subject to class accessibility.

question_text: Can a protected member be accessed by a subclass in another package?
explanation: A protected member can be accessed in a subclass in another package through the applicable subclass access rules.

question_text: Which statement about importing packages is correct?
option_a: Importing a package copies its source code
option_b: Importing makes types available by their simple names
explanation: An import statement allows types to be referenced by simple name; it does not copy or execute code.

question_text: What is the output? package demo; public class Test { public static void main(String[] args){System.out.println("Package");}}
explanation: The main method prints the string Package when the class is compiled and run correctly.

question_text: What is an exception in Java?
option_b: An event that disrupts normal program execution
explanation: An exception is an event that interrupts the normal flow of program execution.

question_text: Which is the root class of Java's exception and error hierarchy?
explanation: Throwable is the superclass of Exception and Error.

question_text: Which keyword is used to handle an exception?
explanation: The try block contains code that may generate an exception.

question_text: Which block handles an exception generated inside a try block?
explanation: A catch block handles an exception of a matching type.

question_text: Which block normally executes whether an exception occurs or not?
explanation: The finally block generally executes whether or not an exception occurs.

question_text: Which exception occurs when an integer is divided by zero?
explanation: Integer division by zero causes ArithmeticException.

question_text: What is the output? public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){try{int x=10/0;}catch(ArithmeticException e){System.out.print("Error");}}}
explanation: Integer division by zero is caught by the ArithmeticException handler.

question_text: Which exception occurs when accessing a method using a null object reference?
explanation: Calling an instance method through null causes NullPointerException.

question_text: Which exception occurs when converting an invalid numeric string using Integer.parseInt()?
explanation: Invalid integer text causes NumberFormatException.

question_text: What is the difference between checked and unchecked exceptions?
option_a: Checked exceptions are checked at compile time; unchecked exceptions are not required to be caught or declared
option_b: Unchecked exceptions are always checked by the compiler
explanation: Checked exceptions are subject to compile-time handling requirements; unchecked exceptions are runtime exceptions.

question_text: Which is a checked exception?
explanation: IOException is a checked exception.

question_text: Which is an unchecked exception?
explanation: NullPointerException is a subclass of RuntimeException and is unchecked.

question_text: What happens if an exception is not handled?
option_b: It propagates and may terminate the thread
explanation: An uncaught exception propagates up the call stack and may terminate the thread.

question_text: Which exception occurs when accessing an invalid array index?
explanation: Accessing an array outside its valid index range causes ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.

question_text: What is the output? public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){try{int[] a={1,2}; System.out.print(a[3]);}catch(ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException e){System.out.print("Invalid");}}}
explanation: Index 3 is invalid for an array of length 2, so the catch block executes.

question_text: Which class represents exceptions that applications can commonly handle?
explanation: Exception represents conditions that applications may catch and handle.

question_text: Which class is the superclass of RuntimeException?
explanation: RuntimeException extends Exception.

question_text: Which exception can occur when converting an incompatible object reference using a cast?
explanation: An incompatible reference cast can cause ClassCastException.

question_text: What is the output? public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){try{System.out.print("A");}catch(Exception e){System.out.print("B");}finally{System.out.print("C");}}}
explanation: The try block prints A and the finally block prints C. The catch block is skipped.

question_text: Can a try block have multiple catch blocks?
explanation: A try block can have multiple catch blocks to handle different exception types.

question_text: What is the correct order when using related exception types in multiple catch blocks?
explanation: Specific subclass exceptions must be caught before their superclass to avoid unreachable catch blocks.

question_text: What is the output? try{int x=10/0;}catch(NullPointerException e){System.out.print("N");}catch(ArithmeticException e){System.out.print("A");}
explanation: ArithmeticException matches the second catch block.

question_text: What is a multi-catch block?
option_a: One catch handling multiple exception types
explanation: Multi-catch uses a single catch block with multiple exception types separated by vertical bars.

question_text: What is a nested try block?
option_a: A try block inside another try block
option_c: A finally block inside a method
option_d: A try block inside an interface
explanation: A nested try block is a try block placed inside another try block.

question_text: Can an inner try block have its own catch block?
explanation: An inner try block can independently handle exceptions using its own catch block.

question_text: What is the output? try{try{int x=10/0;}catch(ArithmeticException e){System.out.print("Inner");}}catch(Exception e){System.out.print("Outer");}
explanation: The inner catch handles the exception, so the outer catch does not execute.

question_text: Which keyword explicitly throws an exception object?
explanation: The throw keyword explicitly throws an exception object.

question_text: Which statement correctly throws an IllegalArgumentException?
explanation: The throw statement requires an exception object created using new.

question_text: What is the purpose of the throws keyword?
option_b: To declare exceptions that a method may pass to its caller
explanation: throws declares possible exceptions in a method signature.

question_text: Which keyword is used inside a method to explicitly raise an exception?
explanation: throw is used to explicitly raise an exception.

question_text: Which keyword appears in a method declaration?
explanation: throws appears in the method declaration after its parameter list.

question_text: What happens? throw new ArithmeticException();
explanation: The statement throws an ArithmeticException unless it is caught by an applicable handler.

question_text: Does declaring an exception with throws automatically handle it?
explanation: throws declares propagation; it does not handle the exception.

question_text: Which method declaration correctly declares IOException?
explanation: The throws clause follows the method parameter list.

question_text: What is the output? public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){try{throw new RuntimeException();}catch(RuntimeException e){System.out.print("Caught");}}}
explanation: The explicitly thrown RuntimeException is caught by the matching catch block.

question_text: What happens if an exception thrown inside a method is not caught there but is declared using throws?
option_a: It can propagate to the caller
explanation: The caller becomes responsible for handling or further declaring a checked exception.

question_text: Can a method declare more than one exception using throws?
explanation: A throws clause can declare multiple exception types separated by commas.

question_text: What is the output? try{System.out.print("A"); throw new Exception();}catch(Exception e){System.out.print("B");}finally{System.out.print("C");}
explanation: A is printed before the exception, B in the catch block, and C in finally.

question_text: What is the primary purpose of a finally block?
explanation: finally is commonly used for cleanup operations such as releasing resources.

question_text: Does a finally block normally execute when a return statement is executed inside try?
explanation: The finally block normally executes before the method returns.

question_text: Can a try block exist without catch if it has finally?
explanation: Java permits try-finally without a catch block.

question_text: Can a finally block exist without a try block?
explanation: A finally block must be associated with a try statement.

question_text: What is the output? try{System.out.print("Try");}finally{System.out.print("Finally");}
explanation: The try block executes first, followed by finally.

question_text: What is the output? try{System.out.print("A"); return;}finally{System.out.print("B");}
explanation: The finally block executes before the method returns, producing AB.

question_text: In which situation might a finally block not execute?
explanation: Abrupt JVM termination, such as System.exit(), can prevent finally from executing.

question_text: What is a user-defined exception?
option_a: An exception created by the programmer
explanation: Programmers can define custom exception classes for application-specific conditions.

question_text: Which class can be extended to create a checked user-defined exception?
explanation: Extending Exception creates a checked custom exception unless a runtime exception superclass is used.

question_text: Which class can be extended to create an unchecked user-defined exception?
explanation: A custom exception extending RuntimeException is unchecked.

question_text: What is the output? class AgeException extends Exception {} public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){try{throw new AgeException();}catch(AgeException e){System.out.print("Invalid Age");}}}
explanation: The custom checked exception is thrown and caught.

question_text: What must a custom checked exception generally do when thrown from a method?
explanation: Checked exceptions must be caught or declared using throws.

question_text: Which constructor can pass a message to the superclass Exception?
explanation: super(message) invokes the superclass constructor that stores the exception message.

question_text: Which method returns the detail message of an exception?
explanation: getMessage() returns the detail message associated with the exception.

question_text: What is the purpose of getCause() in Throwable?
option_a: To return the original cause of an exception
explanation: getCause() returns the underlying cause, if one has been set.

question_text: What is exception propagation?
option_a: Passing an unhandled exception up the call stack
option_b: Converting an exception to a variable
explanation: An exception propagates through method calls until a matching handler is found.

question_text: What happens if an exception is thrown in a catch block and not handled there?
option_b: It propagates to an enclosing handler or caller
explanation: An exception thrown inside catch can propagate outward if not handled.

question_text: Can a finally block itself throw an exception?
explanation: Code inside finally can throw exceptions, potentially affecting exception propagation.

question_text: What is try-with-resources primarily used for?
explanation: Try-with-resources automatically closes supported resources when the statement finishes.

question_text: Which interface must a resource implement to be used in try-with-resources?
explanation: Resources used in try-with-resources must implement AutoCloseable.

question_text: What is a byte stream mainly used for?
explanation: Byte streams handle raw 8-bit data and are useful for binary files.

question_text: Which is the base class for byte input streams?
explanation: InputStream is the abstract base class for byte input streams.

question_text: Which is the base class for byte output streams?
explanation: OutputStream is the abstract base class for byte output streams.

question_text: Which class reads bytes from a file?
explanation: FileInputStream reads raw bytes from a file.

question_text: Which class writes bytes to a file?
explanation: FileOutputStream writes raw bytes to a file.

question_text: Which method reads the next byte from an InputStream?
explanation: read() reads one byte and returns -1 when the stream reaches the end.

question_text: What does InputStream.read() return when the end of the stream is reached?
explanation: The read() method returns -1 to indicate the end of the stream.

question_text: Which method writes a byte or byte array to an OutputStream?
explanation: write() sends byte data to the output stream.

question_text: What are character streams designed to handle?
explanation: Character streams are designed for reading and writing text.

question_text: Which is the base class for character input streams?
explanation: Reader is the abstract base class for character input streams.

question_text: Which is the base class for character output streams?
explanation: Writer is the abstract base class for character output streams.

question_text: Which class reads characters from a file?
explanation: FileReader reads character data from files.

question_text: Which class writes characters to a file?
explanation: FileWriter writes character data to a file.

question_text: Which class can efficiently read text line by line?
explanation: BufferedReader provides readLine() for reading text lines efficiently.

question_text: Which method reads a complete line using BufferedReader?
explanation: readLine() reads a line of text and returns null at end of stream.

question_text: What is the main difference between byte and character streams?
option_a: Byte streams handle raw bytes; character streams handle text characters
explanation: Byte streams are suitable for binary data, while character streams are intended for text.

question_text: Which stream is generally more suitable for reading an image file?
explanation: Images are binary data and should be read using byte streams.

question_text: Which stream is generally suitable for reading a plain text file?
explanation: FileReader is designed for reading character data from text files.

question_text: What is the purpose of closing an input or output stream?
explanation: Closing a stream releases resources such as file handles.

question_text: Which Java feature can automatically close streams after use?
explanation: Try-with-resources automatically closes resources that implement AutoCloseable.

question_text: What is a thread in Java?
explanation: A thread is a lightweight unit of execution within a process.

question_text: What is multithreading?
explanation: Multithreading allows multiple threads to make progress concurrently.

question_text: Which package contains the Thread class?
explanation: Thread belongs to java.lang, which is automatically imported.

question_text: Which method contains the code executed by a thread?
explanation: The run() method contains the task performed by a thread.

question_text: Which method starts a new thread of execution?
explanation: start() schedules a new thread and causes its run() method to execute.

question_text: What happens when run() is called directly on a Thread object?
option_b: It executes like a normal method call
explanation: Calling run() directly does not start a new thread.

question_text: Which method pauses the currently executing thread for a specified time?
explanation: Thread.sleep() pauses the current thread for the specified duration.

question_text: Which method waits for another thread to finish?
explanation: join() allows one thread to wait until another thread terminates.

question_text: Which method is used to check whether a thread is alive?
explanation: isAlive() returns true if the thread has been started and has not terminated.

question_text: What is the main advantage of multithreading?
explanation: Multithreading can improve responsiveness and concurrency.

question_text: Which method returns the currently executing thread?
explanation: Thread.currentThread() returns the currently executing thread object.

question_text: Which thread is created automatically when a Java program starts?
explanation: The JVM starts execution through the main thread.

question_text: What is the name of the default main thread?
explanation: The initial thread executing the main method is conventionally named main.

question_text: What is the output? public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){System.out.println(Thread.currentThread().getName());}}
explanation: The initial thread normally has the name main.

question_text: Which method sets the name of a thread?
explanation: setName() changes the name of a Thread object.

question_text: Which method returns the name of a thread?
explanation: getName() returns the thread's name.

question_text: What does Thread.sleep(1000) represent?
explanation: The sleep duration is specified in milliseconds.

question_text: Which statement about thread execution order is correct?
option_a: Threads always execute in creation order
explanation: Thread scheduling is controlled by the JVM and operating system, so exact execution order is not guaranteed.

question_text: What is a multi-core processor?
option_a: A processor with multiple processing cores
explanation: A multi-core processor contains multiple processing cores that can execute tasks in parallel.

question_text: Why is multithreading useful in a multi-core system?
option_a: It can use multiple cores for parallel execution
explanation: Multiple threads can execute in parallel on different processor cores.

question_text: Which are the two common ways to create a thread task in Java?
explanation: A class can extend Thread or implement Runnable to define a thread task.

question_text: Which method must be overridden when extending the Thread class to define a task?
explanation: The run() method contains the thread's task.

question_text: Which interface is commonly implemented to define a thread task?
explanation: Runnable defines the run() method for a task executed by a thread.

question_text: Which statement correctly creates a thread using Runnable?
explanation: A Runnable implementation is passed to the Thread constructor.

question_text: What is the output? class MyThread extends Thread { public void run(){System.out.print("Hello");}} public class Main {public static void main(String[] args){new MyThread().start();}}
explanation: The new thread executes run() and prints Hello.

question_text: Can a Java class extend both Thread and another class?
explanation: Java supports single class inheritance, so a class cannot extend both Thread and another class.

question_text: What is the advantage of implementing Runnable?
option_a: The task can be separated from the Thread object
option_c: It removes the need for run()
option_d: It makes a class a package
explanation: Runnable separates the task from the thread and allows the class to extend another class.

question_text: Which constructor can accept a Runnable object?
explanation: Thread has a constructor that accepts a Runnable task.

question_text: Which method returns the current state of a thread?
explanation: getState() returns a Thread.State value.

question_text: Which is a valid Java thread state?
explanation: WAITING is one of the official Java thread states.

question_text: Which thread state indicates that a thread is ready to run or waiting for processor time?
explanation: RUNNABLE includes a thread that is running or ready to run.

question_text: What is the state of a thread before start() is called?
explanation: A newly created thread is in the NEW state.

question_text: What is the state of a thread after its run() method completes?
explanation: A thread enters the TERMINATED state after completing execution.

question_text: Which state indicates that a thread is waiting to enter a synchronized block or method?
explanation: BLOCKED means a thread is waiting to acquire a monitor lock.

question_text: Which method causes the current thread to wait for another thread to complete?
explanation: join() waits for the target thread to terminate.

question_text: Which method can make the current thread pause for a specified time?
explanation: sleep() pauses the currently executing thread.

question_text: What happens if start() is called twice on the same Thread object?
explanation: A Thread object can be started only once.

question_text: Which method requests that the current thread give other threads an opportunity to execute?
explanation: yield() is a scheduling hint that the current thread is willing to yield the processor.

question_text: What is the output? public class Main {public static void main(String[] args){Thread t = new Thread(); System.out.print(t.getState());}}
explanation: The thread has been created but not started, so its state is NEW.

question_text: What is synchronization in Java?
explanation: Synchronization coordinates access to shared resources to prevent race conditions.

question_text: Which keyword is used to synchronize a method or block?
explanation: The synchronized keyword controls access using an object's monitor lock.

question_text: What is a race condition?
option_a: A situation where results depend on unpredictable thread execution timing
explanation: A race condition occurs when concurrent access causes results to depend on execution timing.

question_text: What is the main purpose of a synchronized block?
option_a: To protect a specific section of code
explanation: A synchronized block protects a critical section using a monitor lock.

question_text: Can two threads execute different synchronized instance methods of the same object simultaneously?
explanation: Both synchronized instance methods require the same object's monitor lock.

question_text: Which lock is used by a synchronized static method?
explanation: A synchronized static method locks the Class object associated with the class.

question_text: Which method makes a thread wait and releases the object's monitor lock?
explanation: Object.wait() releases the monitor and waits until notification or another specified condition.

question_text: Which method wakes one waiting thread on the same object monitor?
explanation: notify() wakes one thread waiting on that object's monitor.

question_text: Which method notifies all threads waiting on the same object monitor?
explanation: notifyAll() wakes all threads waiting on the object's monitor.

question_text: Which class provides the wait() and notify() methods?
explanation: wait(), notify(), and notifyAll() are methods of Object.

question_text: From where must wait() normally be called?
option_a: Inside a synchronized context for the same object's monitor
option_d: From any static method without a lock
explanation: The calling thread must own the object's monitor or IllegalMonitorStateException occurs.

question_text: What happens if notify() is called when no threads are waiting on that object?
explanation: If no threads are waiting, the notification is not stored for future waiters.

question_text: Which exception may occur when wait() is interrupted?
explanation: wait() declares InterruptedException.

question_text: What is a critical section?
option_a: A part of code that accesses shared resources
explanation: A critical section is code that requires controlled access to shared data.

question_text: What is the output? class Counter {int count=0; synchronized void increment(){count++;}} What does synchronization help prevent when many threads call increment() on the same object?
option_a: Lost updates caused by concurrent access
explanation: The synchronized method protects the increment operation from concurrent interference on the same object.

question_text: What is the difference between sleep() and wait()?
option_a: sleep() does not release an owned monitor; wait() releases the object's monitor
option_b: sleep() always releases all locks; wait() does not
explanation: sleep() pauses without releasing monitor locks, while wait() releases the monitor on which it is called.

question_text: Which statement about wait() is correct?
option_a: It is a static method of Thread
option_b: It is an instance method of Object
explanation: wait() is defined in Object and is used for inter-thread coordination.

question_text: What can happen if threads acquire multiple locks in conflicting orders?
explanation: Conflicting lock acquisition order can lead to deadlock.

question_text: What is deadlock?
option_a: Threads waiting indefinitely for resources held by each other
explanation: Deadlock occurs when threads cannot proceed because each is waiting for a resource held by another.

question_text: Which statement is recommended when using wait() in a condition-based communication pattern?
option_a: Call wait() inside a loop that checks the condition
option_c: Call notify() before creating any thread
option_d: Call sleep() instead of checking the condition
explanation: A loop rechecks the condition after waking, including after spurious wakeups.

question_text: Which historical Thread method was used to suspend a thread?
explanation: Thread.suspend() historically suspended a thread but is deprecated because it can cause deadlocks.

question_text: Which historical Thread method was used to resume a suspended thread?
explanation: Thread.resume() historically resumed a suspended thread and is deprecated.

question_text: Which historical Thread method was used to stop a thread forcefully?
explanation: Thread.stop() was deprecated because it can leave shared data inconsistent.

question_text: Why are suspend() and resume() deprecated?
option_a: They can cause deadlocks and unsafe synchronization
explanation: Suspending a thread while it holds locks can prevent other threads from proceeding.

question_text: What is a safer way to request that a thread stop its work?
option_a: Use a shared flag and interruption where appropriate
explanation: Cooperative cancellation using a flag or interruption is safer than forcibly stopping a thread.

question_text: Which method can interrupt a thread?
explanation: interrupt() requests interruption of a thread.

question_text: Does interrupt() necessarily terminate a thread immediately?
explanation: Interruption is a cooperative signal; the thread must respond appropriately.

question_text: What is a Java applet in the traditional Java model?
option_a: A small Java program designed to run in an applet-enabled environment
explanation: An applet was traditionally a small Java program embedded in a web page and run by an applet environment.

question_text: Which class was traditionally extended to create a basic applet?
explanation: A basic traditional applet extended java.applet.Applet.

question_text: Which method is called when an applet is first initialized?
explanation: init() performs initial setup when the applet is loaded.

question_text: Which applet lifecycle method is called after initialization and when the applet becomes active?
explanation: start() is called when the applet becomes active.

question_text: Which applet lifecycle method is used to draw output?
explanation: paint(Graphics g) is used to render the applet's visual output.

question_text: Which applet lifecycle method is called when the applet becomes inactive?
explanation: stop() is called when the applet is no longer active.

question_text: Which applet lifecycle method is called before the applet is unloaded?
explanation: destroy() is used for final cleanup before the applet is unloaded.

question_text: Which parameter is passed to the applet paint() method?
explanation: The paint method receives a Graphics object for drawing.

question_text: Which package historically contains the Applet class?
explanation: The traditional Applet class belongs to java.applet.

question_text: Which statement about Java applets today is correct?
option_b: Applets are a modern replacement for HTML
option_c: Applets are obsolete and unsupported by modern browsers
option_d: Applets are required for every Java GUI
explanation: Browser plug-in support for Java applets has been discontinued; applets are legacy technology.

question_text: Which method is used to request repainting of an applet or component?
explanation: repaint() requests that a component be redrawn.

question_text: What is the full form of AWT?
explanation: AWT stands for Abstract Window Toolkit.

question_text: Which package contains Java AWT classes?
explanation: AWT classes are available in the java.awt package.

question_text: Which AWT component is used to display a single line of text?
explanation: Label displays a single line of non-editable text.

question_text: Which AWT component is used to create a clickable button?
explanation: Button represents a clickable GUI button.

question_text: Which AWT component allows the user to enter a single line of text?
explanation: TextField accepts single-line text input.

question_text: Which AWT component supports multiple lines of text?
explanation: TextArea supports multi-line text input and display.

question_text: Which AWT container represents a top-level window?
explanation: Frame is a top-level window with a title bar and border.

question_text: Which method is commonly used to set an AWT window's dimensions?
explanation: setSize() sets the width and height of a component or window.

question_text: Which method makes an AWT component visible?
explanation: setVisible(true) makes the component visible.

question_text: Which interface is commonly used to handle AWT button click events?
explanation: ActionListener handles action events such as button clicks.

question_text: Which method must be implemented by ActionListener?
explanation: ActionListener defines actionPerformed(ActionEvent e).

question_text: Which method registers an ActionListener with a Button?
explanation: addActionListener() registers an action event listener.

question_text: Which class represents an action event in AWT?
explanation: ActionEvent represents an action-related event.

question_text: Which layout manager arranges components in five regions?
explanation: BorderLayout arranges components in North, South, East, West, and Center regions.

question_text: Which layout manager places components sequentially from left to right by default?
explanation: FlowLayout arranges components in a directional flow.

question_text: Which layout manager arranges components in equal-sized rows and columns?
explanation: GridLayout arranges components in a grid of equal-sized cells.

question_text: Which AWT component acts as a general-purpose container for grouping components?
explanation: Panel is a container used to group other GUI components.

question_text: Which method is commonly used to close an AWT Frame after handling its window event?
explanation: dispose() releases the native screen resources associated with a window.

question_text: Which listener interface is commonly used to handle window closing events?
explanation: WindowListener handles window lifecycle events, including closing.

question_text: Which statement correctly describes AWT?
option_a: It provides GUI components and event handling
option_b: It is only used for database connectivity
option_d: It is a Java primitive data type
explanation: AWT provides GUI components, containers, layout managers, and event handling.

question_text: Which keyword declares the exceptions that a method may pass to its caller?
explanation: The throws keyword declares exceptions in a method signature.

question_text: Which Java class is commonly used to read characters from a text file?
explanation: FileReader is a character stream class used to read text.

question_text: Which method should be called to start a new thread in Java?
explanation: The start() method creates a new thread of execution and then invokes its run() method.

question_text: Which method causes the current thread to wait until another thread notifies it?
explanation: The wait() method makes a thread wait until it receives notification or is otherwise interrupted.

question_text: Which method is called when an applet is initialized for the first time?
explanation: The init() method is called once when an applet is first initialized.
